items.content:
중국 규제 당국이 유니트리 로보틱스의 상장 이후 주가 변동성을 계기로 휴머노이드 로봇 스타트업들의 기업공개(IPO) 승인 심사를 대폭 강화하고 나섰다. 모방 업체가 난립하지만, 실질적인 기술적 돌파구는 부족한 과열 시장을 진정시키기 위한 조치다.

9일(현지시간) 디 인포메이션에 따르면, 중국 증권감독관리위원회(CSRC)는 최근 일부 투자은행과 투자사들에 비공식 '창구 지도(window guidance)'를 내려보내 휴머노이드 기업의 IPO 승인 기준을 높이겠다는 입장을 전달했다.

이에 따라 상장을 추진하는 기업들은 지속적인 매출 창출 능력, 적자 축소 가능성, 그리고 실질적인 기술 혁신을 입증해야만 승인받을 수 있게 된다.

창구 지도는 중국 당국이 공식적인 규정 제정 절차를 거치지 않고 금융기관 등에 정책 방향과 기대 수준을 전달하는 방식이다. 이번 조치는 IPO 자체를 차단하기보다는 가격 경쟁과 생산량 확대에만 의존하는 기업을 걸러내, 주식시장에 유사 기업이 과도하게 유입되는 것을 막는 데 초점이 맞춰진 것으로 전해졌다.

중국 휴머노이드 로봇 산업은 올해 들어 폭발적인 투자 열기를 보였다. 크런치베이스에 따르면 올해 상반기 중국 휴머노이드 로봇 스타트업에 유입된 자금은 54억달러(약 7조원)로, 2025년 한 해 동안의 23억달러를 이미 크게 넘어섰다.

중국 기술 컨설팅 업체 애널리시스에 따르면 기업 가치가 20억달러(약 2조7000억원) 이상인 휴머노이드 관련 기업도 10곳을 넘는다.

그러나 민간 시장의 투자 열기와 달리 증시 투자자들의 반응은 냉담하다. 업계 대표주자인 유니트리는 지난달 상하이증권거래소 상장 첫날 주가가 공모가 대비 460% 폭등했지만, 이후 주가가 첫날 종가에서 40% 하락했다. 로봇용 3D 카메라와 소프트웨어를 개발하는 메크마인드 로보틱스도 홍콩증시 상장 이후 공모가보다 약 20% 낮은 수준에서 거래되고 있다.

이런 상황에서도 휴머노이드 기업들의 IPO 추진은 이어지고 있다. 갈봇(GalBot), 애지봇(AgiBot), 림엑스 다이내믹스(LimX Dynamics), 갈락시아 AI(Galaxea AI) 등 여러 업체가 중국 본토 A주 시장이나 홍콩증시 상장을 위한 서류를 제출한 것으로 알려졌다.

규제당국이 기준을 높인 배경에는 중국 전역에서 휴머노이드 스타트업이 우후죽순처럼 늘어난 점도 있다. 업계 추산으로 수백개 기업이 벤처투자를 받았으며, 중국 벤처투자 데이터베이스 IT쥐쯔에 따르면 올해 상반기에 새롭게 탄생한 기업 가치 10억달러 이상의 유니콘 67곳 가운데 19곳이 로봇 분야에 속했다.

문제는 산업 규모가 빠르게 커지는 만큼 기술 발전이 뒤따르지 못하고 있다는 점이다. 일부 기업은 AI 기술을 내세우면서도 실제로는 공장에서 대형 휴머노이드 로봇을 빠르게 생산하는 데 집중하고 있다. 전시회에서는 로봇이 빨래를 개거나 요리를 하고 격투를 벌이는 등 다양한 작업을 수행하는 모습이 공개되지만, 실제 환경에서는 인간의 개입 없이는 작업을 제대로 수행하지 못하는 사례도 적지 않은 것으로 전해졌다.

이에 따라 중국 당국은 휴머노이드 산업의 성장 자체를 억제하기보다는 실제 매출과 기술 경쟁력을 갖춘 기업 중심으로 자본시장의 진입 문턱을 높이는 방향으로 대응하고 있다. 민간 투자에서 시작된 휴머노이드 열풍이 증시로 확대되는 과정에서 실질적인 기술 혁신과 사업 지속 가능성을 입증하지 못하는 기업은 상장 기회를 얻기 어려워질 전망이다.

items.content:
■ 디에스엠(DSM, 104040)이 운영하는 9.81파크 제주가 지난 8월 23억9000만 원의 판매액을 기록하며 2020년 개장 이후 월간 기준 최고치를 경신했다고 밝혔다. 전년 동월 대비 8.0% 증가한 수치로, 파크 내 티켓과 리테일·F&B를 합산한 현장 판매액 기준이다. 8월 9.81파크 제주를 찾은 외국인 이용객은 전년 동월 대비 72.3% 증가했다.

■ KT(대표 박윤영)가 서울아산병원(병원장 박승일)과 ‘AI병원’ 구축에 나선다. 임상 현장에 적용 가능한 AI 의료서비스 개발을 위한 AX협력을 추진한다고 밝혔다. AI병원이 구현되면 서울아산병원에 환자가 내원했을 때 AI가 영상 판독을 지원, 여러 시스템에 흩어진 건강기록을 자동으로 수집·분석해줄 것으로 전망했다.

■ 노르마(대표 정현철)가 국내 양자 산업 전시회 ‘2026 국제양자산업대전’에 참가해 QLLM, Q 플랫폼 MCP 등 자체 개발 양자 AI 기술을 선보였다. 지난 7월 출시한 Q 플랫폼 MCP는 챗GPT, 클로드 등 생성 AI와 노르마의 양자 프로그램을 연결한 서비스다. 별도 소프트웨어 개발 도구(SDK)나 양자 프로그래밍 라이브러리를 설치하지 않아도 AI에 자연어 명령어를 입력해 양자 알고리즘을 작성하고 실행 결과를 확인할 수 있다.

■ 에이아이웍스(대표 윤석원)가 환경경영시스템 국제표준인ISO 14001:2015(KS I ISO 14001:2015)인증을 취득했다고 밝혔다. AI산업의 전력·연산 자원 소비가 빠르게 늘어나는 가운데, 데이터 구축부터 AI에이전트 개발에 이르는 AI밸류체인 단계를 환경경영 관리 체계 안에 편입했다. 이번 인증은 한국경영인증원(KMR)의 문서심사와 현장심사를 거쳐 지난 8월14일자로 이뤄졌다.

■ AI 금융 전문 어피닛(AFINIT, 대표 이철원)이 한국 스타트업의 인도 진출을 지원하는 프로젝트 '프리 유니콘 인디아'를 가동, 그 첫 번째 프로그램으로 '한국 스타트업 인도 시장조사 프로그램'을 시작한다고 밝혔다. 인도 시장 진출에 관심 있는 한국 스타트업 대표 4인을 선발해 오는 10월22일부터 27일까지 인도 델리 현지에서 진행된다. 지원자는 인도 사업 구상서를 제출해야 하며, 화상 인터뷰를 거쳐 최종 4개사가 선발될 예정이다.

■ AI 커뮤니케이션 교육 솔루션 전문 크디랩은 직무 화법 코칭 플랫폼 ‘쏘카인드(Sokind)’에 커스텀 AI 롤플레이 기능을 추가했다고 밝혔다. 커스텀 AI 롤플레이는 사용자가 실제 업무에서 만날 고객의 특성과 상황을 직접 설정해 AI 고객과 대화를 연습하는 기능이다. 현장 직원이 자신에게 필요한 상황을 직접 만들어 연습할 수 있도록 개인화 범위를 넓힌 것이 특징이다.

■ 서울 AI 허브는 캐나다 몬트리올 소재 딥테크 액셀러레이터 센테크(Centech) 와 AI 스타트업의 글로벌 진출과 공동 육성을 위한 MOU를 체결했다고 밝혔다. 서울 AI 스타트업의 캐나다 시장 진출을 위한 현지 협력 기반을 마련하고, 기술 실증(PoC)부터 오픈이노베이션, 현지 파트너 발굴과 투자·연구 네트워크까지 연결하는 글로벌 사업화 지원체계를 구축하기 위해 마련됐다.

■ 레디앤스타트(대표 조윤진)가 운영하는 커리어 플랫폼 잇다(itdaa)의 AI 진단검사 누적 이용 건수가 1만건을 달성했다고 밝혔다. 지난해 4월 잇다가 출시한 AI 진단검사는 개인의 성향과 역량을 분석해 자신에게 적합한 직무를 탐색하도록 도움을 준다. 이용자는 검사 결과를 참고해 관심 직무를 살펴보고, 해당 분야 현직자에게 실제 업무와 필요한 역량, 준비 방법을 질문할 수 있다.

■ 메가존클라우드(대표 염동훈)의 관계사 메가존소프트는 글로벌 화장품 제조자개발생산(ODM) 기업 씨앤씨인터내셔널에 구글 워크스페이스 기반 AI 전환(AX) 시스템을 구축했다고 밝혔다. 임직원이 구글 워크스페이스의 주요 기능을 실무에 활용할 수 있도록 실습 중심 교육도 함께 제공했다.

items.content:
최초의 AI 코딩 에이전트 ‘데빈(Devin)’을 개발한 코그니션(Cognition)이 불과 4개월 만에 기업 가치를 크게 높이며 또 한 번 대규모 자금 조달에 성공했다.

코그니션은 9일(현지시간) 20억달러(약 2조7000억원) 규모의 시리즈E 투자를 유치하며 기업 가치를 480억달러(약 64조원)로 끌어올렸다고 발표했다. 지난 5월 260억달러의 가치로 10억달러 이상을 조달한 지 불과 4개월 만에 몸값이 85% 급증한 것이다.

이번 투자 라운드는 신규 투자자인 앤드리슨 호로위츠(a16z)와 액셀이 공동 주도했으며, 피터 틸의 파운더스 펀드, 제너럴 캐털리스트, 아베니어 등 기존 투자자들도 참여했다. 알티미터와 베인캐피털벤처스 등도 투자자로 이름을 올렸다.

코그니션의 가치 급등은 AI 코딩 시장이 단일 기업이 독점하는 시장이 아니라 여러 대형 사업자가 상당한 시장 점유율을 확보할 수 있는 분야라는 투자업계의 판단에 따른 것이다. 특히 단순한 코드 자동완성을 넘어 실제 소프트웨어 개발 업무를 자율적으로 수행하는 단계로 발전하면서 성장성이 높게 평가되고 있다.

대표 제품인 ‘데빈(Devin)’은 2024년 최초의 코딩 에이전트로 소개되며 화제를 모은 제품이다. 코드를 작성하는 것은 물론 소프트웨어 개발 과정에서 다양한 작업을 독립적으로 수행할 수 있도록 설계됐다.

연간 반복 매출(ARR)은 지난 5월 4억9200만달러에서 최근 9억달러(약 1조2000억원)로 증가했다. 몇 달 만에 83% 늘어난 것으로, 기업들의 AI 코딩 도구 도입이 빠르게 확대되고 있음을 보여준다. 엔비디아의 반도체 설계와 GE에어로스페이스의 항공 분야, 씨티의 금융 서비스, 메르세데스-벤츠의 자동차 사업, 모달의 AI 인프라 등 다양한 산업의 엔지니어링 조직에서 활용되고 있다고 설명했다.

올해 초에는 아시아·태평양 지역으로 사업을 확대할 계획도 밝혔다. 호주와 뉴질랜드, 인도뿐 아니라 한국 시장도 진출 대상에 포함됐다.

The world needs far more software than it can build. Cognition exists to change that. We’ve just raised over $2B at a $48B valuation, led by a16z, Accel, Founders Fund, General Catalyst, and Avenir. Since our round in May, run-rate revenue has grown from $492 M to almost $900… pic.twitter.com/Z7Ph29GG6B

다만 고비용 구조는 과제로 꼽힌다. 엔비디아 서버를 임대하는 데 연간 수억달러를 지출하는 것으로 알려졌으며, 올해 전체 현금 소진액이 8억달러(약 1조원)에 이를 수 있다는 분석도 나왔다. AI 코딩 서비스가 대규모 컴퓨팅 자원을 필요로 하는 만큼, 매출 증가와 함께 추론 비용을 얼마나 효율적으로 관리하느냐가 수익성 확보의 핵심이 될 전망이다.

비용 절감을 위해 오픈소스 모델을 기반으로 자체 AI 모델을 개발하고 있다. 장기적으로 오픈AI와 앤트로픽 등 외부 AI 모델에 대한 의존도를 낮추면 컴퓨팅 비용을 줄이고 손익분기점에 근접하겠다는 전략이다.

올해 말까지 ARR 40억~50억달러(약 5조3000억~6조7000억원)를 달성할 것으로 예상하고 있다. 경쟁사인 커서는 올해 연말 ARR이 60억달러(약 8조원)를 넘어설 것으로 전망된 바 있다.

items.content:
AI 음악 생성 스타트업 수노(Suno)가 워너뮤직그룹, BMG와 협력해 정식 라이선스를 확보한 음악을 기반으로 새로운 음악을 생성할 수 있는 AI 모델을 출시했다.

수노는 9일(현지시간) 워너뮤직그룹 및 BMG와 협력해 개발한 ‘v6’ 세대 AI 음악 모델 제품군을 공개했다.

참여 아티스트의 라이선스 음악에서 영감받아 새로운 음악을 만들 수 있도록 설계됐으며, 기존 모델보다 빠르고 높은 품질의 결과물을 제공하는 것이 특징이다.

프로와 프리미어 가입자는 v6와 실험적인 ‘v6-와일드(Wild)’를 사용할 수 있다. v6는 특정한 창작 목표에 맞춰 정교하게 음악을 생성하는 데 초점을 맞추며, v6-와일드는 다양한 아이디어를 탐색하고 예상하지 못한 음악적 결과를 만들어내는 용도로 설계됐다.

무료 이용자를 위한 ‘v6-미니(mini)’도 제공된다. 기존 무료 음악 생성 모델보다 빠르고 뛰어난 결과를 제공할 것이라는 설명이다.

구체적인 지급 규모는 공개되지 않았다. 수노가 음반사와 음악 출판사에 비용을 지급하면, 각 회사가 해당 수익을 아티스트와 작곡가에게 배분하는 방식이다. 마이키 슐먼 창립자 겸 CEO는 "앞으로 아티스트가 직접 참여 여부를 선택하고, 참여할 경우 보상을 받을 수 있는 새로운 형태의 제품도 개발하고 있다"고 밝혔다.

Welcome to the v6 era. Our best models yet, built in partnership with artists and producers. Here’s how the family works pic.twitter.com/Lwj5jRSCLJ

음악 생성 방식도 확대했다. 이용자는 텍스트 프롬프트뿐 아니라 오디오, 이미지, 동영상에서 영감받아 곡을 만들 수 있으며, 하나의 프롬프트에서 여러 장르와 음악적 요소를 결합한 곡을 생성할 수도 있다.

AI 음악 시장에서는 기존 곡을 AI로 리믹스하거나 커버하는 기능에 대한 관심도 높아지고 있다. 스포티파이도 라이선스 음악을 기반으로 새로운 버전을 만들고 팬들과 공유할 수 있는 AI 리믹스 도구를 개발하고 있다. 수노도 유사한 기능을 개발 중이다.

items.content:
기후·에너지 커뮤니케이션 전문 기후미디어허브가 여론조사 기관 엠브레인에 의뢰해 전국 만 20~69세 남녀 5000명을 대상으로 실시한 조사 결과, 반도체 클러스터·AI 데이터센터 등 ‘3대 메가프로젝트’ 사용 전력의 일정 비율 이상을 재생에너지로 공급하도록 의무화하는 제도에 63.2%가 찬성하는 것으로 집계됐다.

응답자의 67.8%가 3대 메가프로젝트 추진 자체를 긍정적으로 평가했으며, 프로젝트 추진을 위한 필요 요소로 ‘전문 인력 양성’(30.6%)에 이어 ‘안정적인 전력 확보’(20.7%)를 최우선 과제로 꼽았다.

전력원으로 원자력을 최우선으로 확대해야 한다고 답한 응답층에서도 의무화 찬성(48.3%)이 반대(21.6%)보다 두 배 이상 높았다. 기후·에너지 이슈 관심 및 디지털 행동 활성층에서는 찬성률이 75.3%로 더 높게 나타났다.

연령별로는 50대(70.0%), 60대(69.4%), 40대(63.2%) 순으로 40대 이상에서 특히 높았다.

가장 시급하게 확대해야 할 에너지원으로는 재생에너지(태양광·풍력 등)가 49.6%로 1위를 차지했고, 원자력(35.9%)이 뒤를 이었다. LNG 등 가스발전 확대 응답은 3.5%에 그쳤다.

세명대 저널리즘대학원 부설 저널리즘연구소 제정임 교수는 "재생에너지에 대한 국민 인식이 산업경쟁력과 에너지 안보를 위해 필요한 전력원이라는 실용적 지지로 확장되고 있다"며 "원전이냐 재생에너지냐 하는 제로섬 정쟁에서 벗어나 실용적인 에너지 믹스를 수용하는 인식이 확산되고 있다는 점에서 긍정적인 변화"라고 강조했다.

한편, 이번 조사는 7월27일부터 29일까지 온라인으로 실시했다. 표본은 성·연령·지역 기준 인구비례 할당으로 표본오차는 95% 신뢰수준에서 약 ±1.4%p다.

items.summary: 딥시크가 중국 본토 기업공개(IPO)를 추진하기 위해 씨틱증권(CITIC Securities)을 주관사로 선정한 것으로 알려졌다. 상하이증권거래소의 기술 기업 중심 시장인 스타마켓(STAR Market) 상장을 위한 절차에 착수할 계획으로, 딥시크의 IPO 추진이 구체적인 단계에 접어들었다는 신호로 풀이된다.로이터는 9일(현지시간) 딥시크가 최근 씨틱증권을 IPO 준비를 위한 증권사로 선정했으며, 올해 안에 IPO 절차를 시작하는 것을 목표로 하고 있다고 보도했다.본토 증시 상장을 추진하는 기업들
items.content:
딥시크가 중국 본토 기업공개(IPO)를 추진하기 위해 씨틱증권(CITIC Securities)을 주관사로 선정한 것으로 알려졌다. 상하이증권거래소의 기술 기업 중심 시장인 스타마켓(STAR Market) 상장을 위한 절차에 착수할 계획으로, 딥시크의 IPO 추진이 구체적인 단계에 접어들었다는 신호로 풀이된다.

로이터는 9일(현지시간) 딥시크가 최근 씨틱증권을 IPO 준비를 위한 증권사로 선정했으며, 올해 안에 IPO 절차를 시작하는 것을 목표로 하고 있다고 보도했다.

본토 증시 상장을 추진하는 기업들은 통상 증권사를 선정해 상장 전 지도 및 준비 작업을 진행한 뒤 공식적인 상장 신청에 들어간다.

실제 상장 시점과 공모 규모, 기업 가치 등 구체적인 조건은 아직 결정되지 않은 것으로 알려졌다. 딥시크와 씨틱증권은 관련 논평 요청에 답변하지 않았다.

딥시크는 상장과 추가 자금 조달을 통해 대규모 컴퓨팅 인프라를 확충하고 AI 모델 개발에 투자하는 한편, 핵심 연구 인력의 이탈을 막고 우수 인재를 추가로 확보하려는 것으로 전해졌다.

IPO에 앞서 대규모 자금 조달도 진행하고 있다. 현재 750억달러(약 100조원)의 가치로 신규 투자 라운드를 진행 중이다. 지난 6월에도 74억달러(약 10조원)의 자금을 조달했으며, 투자 이후 기업 가치는 500억달러(약 67조원)를 넘어선 것으로 알려졌다.

딥시크를 비롯해 중국 AI 스타트업은 자금 조달 경쟁에 나서고 있다. AI 모델 경쟁이 고도화되면서 고성능 컴퓨팅, 데이터센터, 연구개발 인력 확보에 막대한 비용이 필요해졌기 때문이다. 지푸 AI(Z.ai)와 미니맥스는 올해 홍콩 증시에 이미 상장했으며, 문샷 AI도 비공개로 홍콩 IPO를 신청한 것으로 알려졌다.

중국 AI 기업들의 몸값은 빠르게 높아지고 있지만, 미국 경쟁사와 비교하면 여전히 상당한 격차가 존재한다. 딥시크가 750억달러 수준으로 평가되는 가운데, Z.ai의 시가총액은 540억달러(약 72조원) 수준이다.

반면 앤트로픽은 IPO 과정에서 최대 2조달러(약 2678조원)의 가치가 거론되고 있으며, 오픈AI도 1조달러(약 1339조원) 이상의 평가가 목표다.

이 같은 차이는 AI 기술력뿐 아니라 매출과 수익화 수준의 격차를 반영한다. 중국 AI 기업들이 글로벌 수준의 모델 성능을 확보하더라도 이를 실제 매출과 이익으로 전환하는 데에는 여전히 어려움이 있다는 것이다.

딥시크가 중국 본토 증시의 스타마켓을 선택한 것도 주목된다. 홍콩이 아닌 상하이에서 IPO를 추진하면 중국 정부가 전략산업으로 육성하는 AI 분야의 대표 기업으로서 국내 자본시장에서 자금 확보에 유리하다는 분석이다.

items.title: Volvo cancels EX40 in the US, updates XC40 with better sensors and Gemini AI
items.summary: Today, Volvo said it was canceling the entry-level electric EX40 in the US, while also giving its aging hybrid XC40 a new look. When it arrives at dealerships early next year, the new XC40 will have updated exterior styling, a gut-renovated interior featuring Google's Gemini AI a
items.content:
The compact EX40 struggled to find customers. But the hybrid version of Volvo’s small XC40 SUV is getting a facelift.

Today, Volvo said it was canceling the entry-level electric EX40 in the US, while also giving its aging hybrid XC40 a new look. When it arrives at dealerships early next year, the new XC40 will have updated exterior styling, a gut-renovated interior featuring Google’s Gemini AI assistant, enlarged infotainment screen, and a new sensor-and-software safety suite.

Volvo is expected to replace the EX40 with the slightly larger EX50, riding on the automaker’s lower-cost SPA3 platform. The EV should reach US dealerships by mid-2027, and will likely start in the high-$40,000 range, according to Automotive News .

As a hybrid, the XC40 serves as a bridge for customers who want better gas mileage but aren’t ready for the pure EV lifestyle. Volvo itself needs that bridge, after backing down from its pledge to sell only EVs by 2030. That said, the automaker didn’t divulge any details about the powertrain, engine options, electric motor, range, or battery capacity for the XC40 — so we’ll have to wait and see whether this SUV can sufficiently compete in an increasingly cutthroat hybrid market .

On the surface, we’ve got a new take on Volvo’s signature “Thor’s Hammer” LED headlights, as well as an updated front grille, bumper, hood and front wings. Same goes for the rear: new lighting, new bumper, and an upgraded tailgate. Additionally, the XC40 is getting a trio of diamond-cut wheel options, available in 18-, 19-, and 20-inch sizes.

But the interior is where the meat of Volvo’s improvements comes through. The screen has been bumped up to a higher resolution and a larger, 11.2-inch size. It will run Volvo’s latest user interface, which the automaker designed for faster navigation with fewer taps. Google’s Gemini serves as the voice assistant , using its big AI brain to plan routes, find specific locations and detours, and manage messages. The XC40 rounds it out with an improved wireless phone charger and smart storage solutions.

What about safety? This is a Volvo after all, the automaker most committed to Safety (at least according to its well-cultivated reputation). Don’t worry, the XC40 ups the ante in that department with a new software and sensor platform that’s designed to provide real-time collision avoidance, automated emergency steering, and automatic emergency braking.

The sensor upgrade includes new front and corner radars, a new front camera, new rear corner radars, 12 new ultrasonic sensors, and new parking cameras. Cloaked in this new sensor suite, the XC40 is getting a host of new safety capabilities, including new door opening alerts that warn occupants before dooring passing cyclists, lane change assist and smoother lane following support on long drives, and an optional 3D/360-degree camera to simplify low-speed maneuvering and parking.

The ultimate goal is to build a better XC40 — one that’s safer and more capable, which hopefully translates to better sales numbers and a long, continuous shelf life for Volvo’s tiny SUV.

“By enhancing the XC40’s design, technology and safety features, we’ve created the best version of the XC40 yet,” says Akhil Krishnan, Interim Lead for the 30 and 40 Series at Volvo Cars, in a statement. “This already popular model is now set to continue being one of our best-selling cars for years to come.”

Correction September 10th: A previous version of this story described the new XC40 as a plug-in hybrid. It is a mild hybrid.

Update September 10th: Updated to include information about the canceling of the EX40.

GitHub availability report: August 2026
items.summary: In August, we experienced five incidents that resulted in degraded performance across GitHub services. The post GitHub availability report: August 2026 appeared first on The GitHub Blog .
items.content:
While we continue to make progress, August proved to be a challenging month for availability. You can read more about these incidents in a blog post we published last month. We are aggressively investing in both architectural improvements and moving to Azure, which will give us more capacity. Meanwhile, we continue to see significant growth on our platform. We are prioritizing the most impactful work while minimizing risk, but as these incidents in August show, we cannot completely eliminate risk.

Ultimately, all the work needs to be done, and incidents give us an opportunity to adjust our priorities. As repair items from these incidents, we’ve made significant improvements to our capacity monitoring and management, retry policies that led to bigger impact, and resiliency improvements to core services. We’ve also continued to make great progress across many durable work streams.

On August 11, GitHub ran a production MySQL primary from Azure for the first time. Client-observed write impact was minimal, and no customer impact occurred in the transition. We repeated the pattern with two more primaries on August 27. We have further primaries scheduled over the coming weeks, increasing in complexity as we learn from each failover.

Read traffic also reached new highs. Reads from migrated services peaked at 60.4%, while reads from GitHub’s monolith peaked at 64.3% in Azure. Git reads reached 54%.

Away from the regional migration, the 24-table authentication-core cohort moved off GitHub’s oldest shared database, mysql1, removing approximately one million queries per second from its replicas. Separate query-hygiene changes removed another 120,000 queries per second and eliminated approximately 59,000 seconds of wasted database work per hour.

GitHub Actions gained additional capacity while longer-term isolation work continues. Job-routing changes moved 33% of jobs from a constrained production cluster to spare capacity, reducing peak cache CPU utilization from 98% to 80% and adding an estimated three months of headroom. This is a near-term containment measure, not the finish line; the August outage reinforced the need for more durable capacity and isolation, which continues.

Pull request isolation work continued. In addition to unauthenticated traffic already being served, now authenticated reads for the first production cohort reached 100%.

Investments in Git overload protection served 6.4% more traffic while improving 95th-percentile duration by 24% and maximum delay by 78%. Broader load-shedding protections at the edge also made progress, enabling levers that can protect GitHub under unexpected load—in fact, these protections were used in mitigating the aforementioned incidents in August.

We also improved monitoring and telemetry. Pull request monitoring now measures merge, review, and comment failures independently, where high read volume could otherwise mask a failing write path. On August 21, automated high impact incident detection began combining customer-support signals with service telemetry. API monitoring was also recalibrated and validated over 30 days, reducing noise and improving signal quality. These changes improve detection and response.

The next month of work includes moving the next database primaries, continuing to migrate services and corresponding traffic to Azure, chipping away at database health particularly on shared-databases, adding more automation around capacity management and auto-scaling, and extending dependency-failure handling across more of the pull request experience.

This principle continues to guide us: availability, then capacity, then features.

The incident began with a routine deployment to an internal GitHub Actions service that processes incoming events and turns them into actions jobs. The deployment’s contents were not at fault (we rolled it back to confirm this); instead, replacing pods during the rollout briefly reduced capacity in one site and pushed the remaining sites past their limit as traffic shifted to them. Impact was heaviest through the middle hours of the incident, when a large share of actions workflow runs were failing to start or complete.

The affected actions services were running close to their capacity and concurrency limits. A routine deployment that briefly reduced the number of running pods was enough to exhaust available headroom. This caused service mesh sidecars to experience CPU throttling and out-of-memory restarts, which then cascaded into cache, DNS, and API errors across multiple clusters. The ingress service mesh for these services had limited headroom so it could not absorb the temporary loss of capacity during the deployment.

As the core services recovered, a latent bug in the job-assignment path made recovery slower: runners were handed jobs that had already been revoked, then got stuck retrying them instead of picking up valid work, which created a self-amplifying backlog.

A new peak in traffic pushed one datacenter’s load balancers past their limits. A service-mesh sidecar reached its concurrency limit and did not scale up.

As requests backed up, several of the datacenter’s load-balancer nodes exhausted their network flow limits, which degraded the shared gateway authentication path and produced widespread authentication latency and failures across the many services that route through that datacenter.

A latent client retry bug sharply amplified traffic to one internal authentication endpoint, which slowed recovery for the Copilot Token Service. The core weakness was that our service-mesh sidecar did not scale up, together with our retry behavior, and clients were not bound enough to keep a partial degradation from amplifying into a broader overload.

items.title: AI research startup Listen Labs scrubbed a $1.5B funding round for Salesforce talks
items.summary: Listen Labs walked away from a signed Series C term sheet from Menlo Ventures, sources say.
items.content:
Listen Labs, a market research startup that uses voice AI to conduct customer interviews, recently signed a term sheet for a $125 million Series C at a $1.5 billion valuation, with Menlo Ventures set to lead the round, according to several people with knowledge of the matter.

But that round never closed, the people said. Listen Labs walked away from the signed term sheet, a rare occurrence in the venture world and one that is generally frowned upon, according to VCs.

The financing likely collapsed because of acquisition talks with Salesforce. The CRM giant has recently held talks to buy Listen Labs for around $2 billion , Business Insider reported. The discussions are not finalized, however, and may not result in a deal, the outlet notes.

Listen Labs is one of the leading startups in the rapidly growing field of automating customer research with AI. The three-year-old startup has about $30 million in annualized revenue, about three times more than Simile, a competing startup that predicts human behavior, according to two people familiar with the companies’ financials. In late July, Simile announced that it had closed a $200 million Series B at a $ 2 billion valuation led by Greenoaks — likely setting a new valuation benchmark for Listen Labs, one person said.

If talks with Salesforce collapse, several VCs told TechCrunch that they expect Listen Labs to return to market and target a valuation of $2 billion or higher.

While acquiring Listen Labs could strengthen Salesforce’s AI capabilities by using the startup’s AI to help predict customer needs, the CRM giant may ultimately decide that paying a 67 times revenue multiple is too steep a valuation, according to a person with experience negotiating exits to Salesforce.

Listen Labs, Salesforce, Menlo Ventures, and Simile did not immediately respond to requests for comment.

Listen Labs was co-founded in 2023 by Florian Jüngermann, a former German national champion in competitive computer programming, and Alfred Wahlforss, who previously founded a staffing startup called Bemlo. The two met while pursuing master’s degrees at Harvard.

Listen Labs’ AI develops survey questions and interviews customers over audio or video. The resulting conversations are then packaged into reports and PowerPoint presentations, similar to those traditionally produced by human market researchers.

Fortune 500 companies rely on this type of research to gauge customer needs and satisfaction with their brands and products, but traditional market research is expensive and can take weeks to complete.

Listen Labs’ technology helps reduce the time and cost of these projects, enabling companies to quickly understand how customers are reacting to product changes and iterate on them more efficiently.

The startup’s customers include Microsoft, Canva, Anthropic, and Sweetgreen. Listen Labs and Simile aren’t the only startups using AI to disrupt the customer research market.

Besides Simile, competitors in the space include Outset, Keplar , and Aaru . While some platforms automate interviews with real humans, others startups — like Aaru and Simile — take a synthetic approach, using AI to simulate human behavior and predict responses without interviewing anyone at all.

Listen Labs was previously valued at $500 million when it announced a $69 million Series B round in late January led by Ribbit Capital, with participation from returning backers Sequoia, Conviction, and Pear VC.

items.title: Automattic's board forces CEO Matt Mullenweg into leave of absence
items.summary: Article URL: https://techcrunch.com/2026/09/09/automattics-board-forces-ceo-matt-mullenweg-into-leave-of-absence/ Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49636283 Points: 364 # Comments: 233
items.content:
Matt Mullenweg, the founder and CEO of Automattic, best known as the parent company of WordPress.com, has been put on a leave of absence by his board against his will, according to a Slack message seen by TechCrunch.

Earlier Wednesday, Mullenweg posted in a Slack channel visible to all employees that the company’s Chief Financial Officer, Mark Davies, had “conspired” with other board members Ann Dunwoody, Toni Schneider, and Sue Decker to vote to put Mullenweg on a paid leave of absence.

And the biggest news: I won’t be able to make the [meeting] tomorrow. @Mark Davies has conspired with @Ann Dunwoody, @Toni, and @Sue Decker behind my back and they voted to put me on a paid leave of absence. I voted against that. Wishing Mark and all of you the very best. To clarify @Mark Davies was voted as interim CEO. I received the resolution 50 minutes before the meeting start, and requested repeatedly for time to have it reviewed by independent legal counsel, even a few hours, which was denied.

A Slack message to the open-source WordPress.org community from the project’s executive director, Mary Hubbard, also confirmed Mullenweg’s change of status at the commercial company. However, Hubbard said that WordPress.org was not impacted. “Matt remains the leader of the WordPress project and I remain Executive Director of WordPress. Our teams, priorities, and work continue as planned,” she wrote.

Mullenweg’s Slack message did not make clear why Automattic’s board took this action. Sources told 404 Media , which was the first to report the news, that Schneider — the former CEO of Automattic from 2006 to 2014 — confirmed that the action was initiated by the board. Davies also told employees in the Slack channel that Mullenweg remained on the board of directors.

In an emailed statement to TechCrunch, Automattic confirmed Mullenweg was on leave.

“Matt Mullenweg is currently on leave from Automattic,” the email read. “Mark Davies, Automattic’s CFO, will lead the company as interim CEO. The Board has full confidence in Mark’s leadership and in the team’s ability to execute against the company’s priorities.”

Automattic, which owns other brands including Tumblr, WooCommerce, and Pocket Casts, was founded by Mullenweg in 2003 after he co-created the popular open-source content management system WordPress.

Over the past few years, Mullenweg and the company have been mired in lawsuits and controversy. The company is in a protracted legal battle with WP Engine, a WordPress web hosting competitor. The lawsuit followed allegations from Mullenweg that WP Engine was profiting from the open-source WordPress project without contributing back to the community, and he demanded it pay 8% of its monthly gross revenue as a royalty fee for using the WordPress brand.

WP Engine sued in October 2024 , and accused Automattic and Mullenweg of defamation and abuse of power . Automattic filed counterclaims last year. In February, WP Engine claimed that Automattic intended to target 10 more competitors with royalty claims.

Tensions became so high under Mullenweg’s leadership that he told employees in 2024 to quit, with severance, if they disagreed with him and 159 did so.

Last year, Mullenweg also threatened to deactivate the accounts of several members of the open-source WordPress.org community, after two of them said they planned to spearhead a new forked version of the open source WordPress project.

In April 2025, the company laid off 16% of its staff. The cuts included some longtime employees who had been with the company for more than a decade, sources told TechCrunch.

Some alumni have been asking current employees how they feel about the news, a source told TechCrunch. Some employees said they were “ecstatic” or “relieved” but others had mixed emotions because the move creates more instability.

It isn’t clear why the company’s board made this decision now. One person speculated that the timing may have something to do with Mullenweg’s annual trip to the Burning Man festival, after which he tends to return “with ideas.” This year’s festival ended on September 7.

Mullenweg did not immediately respond to our request for comment.

items.content:
﻿Cameras don’t need to be put in absolutely every product.

September Apple events are always a swirl of information and new, exciting products, and today’s was no different. Apple announced its first foldable, the iPhone Duo, alongside the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max; active noise cancellation (ANC) is now on the cheapest AirPods model, the AirPods 5; and a Siri Recap feature comes to the Watch Series 12 and Watch Ultra 4. But missing were the AirPods Pro with cameras that have been rumored throughout the year and, according to Mark Gurman at Bloomberg , are delayed until 2027 . I’m happy about that and I hope we never get them.

I have too many concerns about a company — any company — putting cameras anywhere, especially in devices like earbuds that are now so ubiquitous in our daily lives. LED lights on glasses or earbuds do little to ease people’s minds when someone is recording them. And some Meta smart glasses users have shown people will hide their recording intentions . While recording in public in the US is generally legal, it can be very creepy. And with earbuds as common as they are, someone could wear them into sensitive situations unnoticed.

Rumors say that the cameras on the potential AirPods will be low-resolution and “aren’t designed” to take images or video , but instead use what they see to inform Siri AI and Visual Intelligence. That information could be used to help with turn-by-turn directions or identify writing and objects like books . Even with a low-resolution camera, it’s still potentially always gathering information about the world (and people!) around you. That invasion of privacy is something I cannot get past.

During today’s event, Apple introduced Audio Intelligence with the Apple Watch, which sounds like a precursor to the Visual Intelligence we’re expecting on the rumored AirPods Pro 4. In its support documentation , Apple points out that audio is not stored and there’s no way to access a recording, which could be the same for video data with Visual Intelligence, and that for its Siri Recap feature, any data used to create a summary is not even accessible by Apple. Any stored data — such as a Siri Recap or a bit of text the user can save with Live Rewind — is also end-to-end encrypted. People are not identified in the Siri Recap, either. Of course, none of this is live yet, so we’ll have to wait and see how well Audio Intelligence works once it’s released.

Functionally, a camera will only gather information if it can see things. What if you have thick, long hair? Or like to wear hoodie sweatshirts? Or fancy, elaborate jewelry? The AirPods would just turn into what they should be — earbuds. It’s possible the reason the AirPods with cameras have been pushed into 2027 is to find solutions to these problems. Or maybe part of the delay is Apple separating itself from the current public climate around cameras thanks to Meta and Flock.

The one immediate benefit of the AirPods with cameras could be accessibility. They could improve situational awareness for people with visual limitations or help hard-of-hearing users read lips. They could even figure out the person you’re speaking to and focus the AirPods’ mics on them for increased intelligibility.

When you take out privacy concerns or the fact that lots of people — and companies — look for opportunities to exploit people, there’s good that can be done. But it involves a lot of trust to be put in untrustworthy hands. I’m not sure I’m ready for that. Or if I ever will be. Whether any of us are ready or not, though, it seems the cameras are coming. The introduction of Apple’s Audio Intelligence on the new Apple Watch is evidence enough that the company is going all in on using sensors to analyze the world around us.

items.summary: Apple has seen reason: It has a black model in the iPhone Pro lineup again. Last year, Apple went bold with its colors for the iPhone 17 Pro, offering a flashy orange, a shiny silver, and a dark blue. Don't get me wrong, they looked nice. But there was no black (or dark gray) for
items.content:
The iPhone 18 Pro comes in four good colors, but there’s only one I care about: black.

Apple has seen reason: It has a black model in the iPhone Pro lineup again.

Last year, Apple went bold with its colors for the iPhone 17 Pro, offering a flashy orange, a shiny silver, and a dark blue. Don’t get me wrong, they looked nice . But there was no black (or dark gray) for the first time since the start of the iPhone Pro lineup, which Apple first introduced in September 2019 with the iPhone 11 Pro and Pro Max.

I care about this because I always buy the black phone. I learned my lesson with the iPhone 6: I got it in gold to mix things up and came to regret it. I don’t need something flashy — I need a phone that blends into the background and looks decent in whatever case I throw it into. After the iPhone 6, my next phone was the iPhone 7 in the excellent matte black (I wasn’t brave enough to endure the jet black model’s potential scratches ), and I’ve only ever gotten the black or gray phones since.

My black titanium iPhone 16 Pro in a black Torras case ( with a mostly black homescreen ) still works very well, thank you very much, and I’m not in the market for a new phone. But when I make my annual mid-September visit to the local Apple Store to look at all the new iPhones, I won’t be rushing to see the iPhone 18 Pro in burgundy, blue, or silver. I’ll be beelining for the model in black.

Just look at this thing! It’s great!

Now Apple, how about a black iPhone Duo ?

items.title: OpenAI adds a prominent AI doomer to its board of directors
items.summary: Paul Christiano, an influential AI researcher focused on alignment, is joining the OpenAI Foundation as a member of its board.
items.content:
Paul Christiano, an influential AI researcher focused on keeping AI systems aligned with human interests and under human control, is joining the OpenAI Foundation board, the frontier lab said Wednesday.

“I now believe there is a meaningful risk that rapid acceleration in AI capabilities leads to catastrophic and irreversible loss of control in the very near term,” Christiano wrote in a social media post . “I do not think that the AI industry in general, including OpenAI, is currently on track to reduce this risk to an acceptable level. I’m joining because I believe that if OpenAI rises to the occasion we could significantly reduce risk.”

Christiano wrote that using AI models to train subsequent AI systems could result in an explosion of capabilities that their creators can’t control.

He joins the board as OpenAI faces renewed scrutiny over its safety procedures, following a series of incidents in which AI agents broke out of restraints and penetrated outside computer systems without the knowledge of OpenAI’s researchers. On Tuesday, Anthropic researcher Jacob Coxon resigned his position to call attention to what he considers irresponsible AI development — and it seems to have worked .

Christiano will join the board’s Safety and Security Committee, led by Carnegie Mellon University professor Zico Kolter. The committee has the final say on whether OpenAI releases new models, like Astra, which was deployed last week. Kolter has not commented publicly on the recent security incidents. OpenAI has not responded to TechCrunch’s request for Kolter’s perspective on the company’s approach to safety following those incidents.

Christiano is one of the people behind reinforcement learning (RL) from human feedback, a key technique for training large language models that he developed while working at OpenAI. He left the lab in 2021, subsequently founding the Alignment Research Center to focus on how to determine if an AI model could threaten its human creators.

“We currently train our AI agents with RL to get as much reward as they can,” he wrote Wednesday. “It has long seemed theoretically possible that this could motivate AI agents to undermine human control, seek power and resources, and cover up their tracks in pursuit of misaligned goals correlated with reward. Public evidence from recent incidents suggests that this is not just a theoretical possibility.”

Sometime in 2024, Christiano became affiliated with the U.S. government’s AI Safety Institute, which later became the Center for AI Standards and Innovation. There, he plays a role in the U.S. government’s largely hidden effort to evaluate frontier AI models before their release.

According to the frontier lab’s announcement, Christiano will continue advising the government while serving in his new role as a board member, but will recuse himself from OpenAI matters and model evaluations. However, that will hardly quell widespread concerns about the AI industry’s influence over policymaking.

items.title: The incomplete history of Duo devices
items.summary: Apple announced the company's first device with a folding screen today, the iPhone Duo, but that's where the firsts end. The Duo is not only far from the first foldable on the market thanks to the efforts of Samsung and Google, but it's also not the first product to be called the
items.content:
﻿Even Apple itself has a history of products called the Duo.

Apple announced the company’s first device with a folding screen today, the iPhone Duo , but that’s where the firsts end. The Duo is not only far from the first foldable on the market thanks to the efforts of Samsung and Google , but it’s also not the first product to be called the Duo.

Former Apple CEO Steve Jobs popularized the saying “good artists copy, great artists steal,” but will the iPhone Duo’s folding screen, which features a custom nano-texture display material to help minimize the visibility of its crease, be enough to make us forget these other Duos that have come before it? Only time, or how aggressively Apple plans to market its Duo, will tell. Is there a Duo we missed? Let us know.

Merging the functionality of the TurboGrafx-16 console and the TurboGrafx-CD that added CD-ROM functionality, the NEC TurboDuo (later rebranded to just the Duo) launched in North America in 1993 after debuting in Japan a few years earlier as the PC Engine Duo. The console was developed as part of a joint venture between NEC and Hudson Soft but never reached the popularity of the original TurboGrafx-16; its short run ended on Christmas Day in 1995.

First released in 2016 and eventually merged into Google Meet in 2022, Google Duo was the company’s proprietary VoIP service meant to compete with products like Skype or Zoom and replace Hangouts. Its cross-platform availability included Android and iOS mobile devices as well as web browsers, and while it supported hi-def video calls, the service was also optimized for slow mobile networks.

The iPhone Duo isn’t even Apple’s first Duo. The PowerBook Duo predates everything Apple announced today by decades. It was an ultraportable laptop, and when Apple introduced it in 1992 it was the smallest and lightest PowerBook available , but still weighed over 4 pounds. Apple managed to shrink the Duo using an approach it still uses today: omitting built-in ports and expansion features. If you wanted to connect peripherals and accessories you had to rely on optional docks. If you’ve ever had to buy a USB hub to connect all your devices to your MacBook, you can thank the PowerBook Duo.

Twenty-three years after the PowerBook Duo was discontinued, the company announced the MagSafe Duo charger that could wirelessly charge an iPhone and an Apple Watch at the same time. However, it felt like a consolation prize for the Apple AirPower wireless charger , which was announced in 2017 but never materialized. The MagSafe Duo was discontinued just a few years later in late 2023, paving the way for the foldable iPhone to steal its identity.

That’s right, the iPhone Duo isn’t even the first folding mobile device to be called the Duo. Microsoft’s Surface Duo launched in 2020 and managed to get around the issues with early foldables like the Samsung Galaxy Fold , which debuted a year prior, by skipping flexible screen technology altogether. Microsoft’s Duo instead had a very visible hinge between its pair of 5.6-inch OLED screens. But software issues, a disappointing camera , and outdated specs when it launched all resulted in the Surface Duo’s failure, even with an improved Duo 2 that launched a year later.

Trade shows are the birthplace of weird laptops, but sometimes the prototypes that often debut just to draw visitors to booths make it into the mainstream. Such was the case with the Asus ROG Zephyrus Duo , a powerful gaming laptop with excellent specs, a wildly expensive price tag, and a pair of 16-inch OLED screens that can be vertically stacked or placed side by side.

The ROG Zephyrus Duo wasn’t Asus’ first attempt at creating a dual-screen laptop, or the first time it named a laptop a Duo. The ZenBook Pro Duo predates it by several years with a slightly different design. Beneath the ZenBook Pro Duo’s primary 15.6-inch OLED screen was a secondary 14-inch display located above the laptop’s keyboard. With an ultrawide 32:9 aspect ratio and less color fidelity, the smaller screen was designed to be a place to dock productivity tools like Slack or Gmail so they were still readily accessible but less of a distraction while working (or gaming) on the primary display.

After convincing Google to open-source the Pebble’s operating system last year, Eric Migicovsky, the creator of what was arguably one of the first truly successful and capable smartwatches, resurrected the wearable under a new company called Core Devices. The Pebble 2 Duo , one of the first smartwatches from Migicovsky’s new company, isn’t as capable as the Apple Watch or devices running Android’s Wear OS, but its careful balance of simplicity, functionality, and a budget-friendly price make it a tempting alternative.

It’s still just a prototype and may never find its way into consumers’ homes, but at IFA 2026 in Berlin last week, iRobot debuted the bizarre Roomba Duo . The prototype includes a beefy mobile dock with clean and dirty water tanks and the most powerful floor-cleaning suction the company has ever made. To ensure it can clean all areas in your home, atop the Roomba Duo is a deployable garage with a smaller Roomba Plus 757 inside that can easily fit into tight spaces and beneath furniture.

Mere hours before the iPhone Duo made its debut, Retroid revealed the full design of its latest dual-screen handheld it’s been teasing. The Retroid Pocket Duo is a modernized version of the Nintendo DS with dual 120Hz OLED screens featuring a 16:9 aspect ratio on top and a 4:3 aspect ratio between its controls. Full specs and pricing aren’t confirmed yet, but the Pocket Duo features a symmetrical dual thumbstick design, two pairs of shoulder buttons, and a headphone jack.

items.title: Apple’s new CEO is reviving a Steve Jobs strategy from 25 years ago
items.summary: John Ternus made the case in his first keynote as Apple CEO that the iPhone isn't going anywhere.
items.content:
Apple CEO John Ternus wants you to know that the iPhone isn’t going anywhere.

Ternus threw his weight behind the venerable device on Wednesday during his first keynote as CEO, placing it firmly at the center of Apple’s product strategy for the AI era.

“There’s no product in the world better designed to be your intelligent personal hub than iPhone,” he said.

This contrasts with the approach taken by former CEO Tim Cook, who tried time and again to convince Wall Street that Apple was more than just the iPhone.

Ternus’ pitch is also a rebuttal to pundits who have recently cast doubt on the iPhone. “The smartphone’s days are numbered,” said one headline . “The Tim Cook era is coming to a close with an existential challenge for Apple: figuring out what comes after the iPhone,” said another article .

But it’s not just about the hardware. Ternus has put the iPhone at the center of his “intelligent personal assistant” strategy , a vision that could define the company for years to come. Steve Jobs did something similar in 2001 with the Mac, less than 10 months before he announced the iPod.

At the time, many observers thought the PC’s days were numbered. At a Macworld New York keynote, Jobs called out bearish quotes from industry wonks like Walt Mossberg and the leaders of Compaq and Gateway.

“This is what everyone else is telling us. That our PC is waning if not the hole being dug,” Jobs said at the time, pointing at a tombstone for the “Beloved PC” on the screen behind him. “We don’t think the PC is dying at all. We don’t think the PC is moving away from the center at all. We think it’s evolving, just like it has since it was invented.”

“We think the PC is on the threshold of entering its third great age,” Jobs added, a prediction driven by the proliferation of digital devices at the time, including camcorders, digital cameras, and DVD players.

The Mac would form the center of a “digital hub” that would connect these disparate devices and, in Jobs’ words, “add value” to all of them.

Later that year, Jobs pulled the iPod out of his pocket, a device seemingly developed to answer the question, “Why do you still need a PC?” The device turned out to be an enormous hit, driving Apple’s profits quarter after quarter and ultimately helping lead to the development of the iPhone.

Today, with the iPhone on the cusp of its 20 th anniversary, Ternus is facing a version of the same question Jobs took on in 2001. We don’t know if Ternus is quietly sitting on an iPod-like product, one that will secure the iPhone’s position a Apple’s hub for years to come. But he is firmly rebutting the idea that the iPhone is past its prime.

“If you were designing the ideal version of this hub from scratch, how would you do it?” Ternus asked, before listing the ingredients: a powerful processor, high-resolution cameras, persistent networking, and on-device AI.

It helps that the iPhone is one of the most powerful personal computing devices around, giving it an edge in the compute-hungry AI era. Its portability and adaptability make it, for many people, the only computing device they need. Even among those who own laptops and iPads, the iPhone is often the one device they can’t live without. Plenty of people leave home without their laptops. Almost no one leaves without their phones.

That combination of power and portability has given Apple a privileged position in the AI world. Other companies have attempted to unseat the iPhone with all manner of wearable devices, but none have succeeded.

Instead of sidelining the iPhone in favor of the next flashy thing, Ternus is leaning into it instead. In a way, he’s bringing Apple around to what the rest of us already know: The iPhone is pretty great, and maybe we don’t need to replace it with something else. Yet.

items.title: Four groups caught using the same Chrome and Windows exploit kit
items.summary: A patch gap and the hastened pace of AI-based vulnerability discovery are likely contributors.
items.content:
A nearly identical exploit kit that targets critical vulnerabilities in both Chromium-based browsers and older versions of Windows is being actively used by at least four hacking groups, some of which have ties to the Chinese government.

Researchers from security firm Proofpoint said Wednesday that BlueMoon, the name they gave to the kit, chains three vulnerabilities together so the attackers using it can install malware of their choice. BlueMoon exploits two Chromium vulnerabilities and one in the kernel of Windows 10 (Oct. 2018 Update), Windows Server 2019, Windows 10 2004, Windows Server 2022, and the initial release of Windows 11. All three vulnerabilities have received patches in the past 24 hours.

The attacks lacked the stealth found in many campaigns. More often, hackers want to exploit newly discovered vulnerabilities sparingly to lengthen their longevity. Proofpoint hypothesized that one reason for the widely used and visible exploit chain was to take advantage of a “patch gap” in the Chromium supply chain, which spans the time a patch is available from developers and the time that patch is incorporated into browsers such as Chrome and Edge. Another likely contributor was the use of AI, which can often spot vulnerabilities faster than discovery performed solely by humans.

Both these factors likely pushed the attackers to move quickly before a window of opportunity closed. Proofpoint said:

A fully weaponized Chrome exploit chain has historically been a high-value, rare capability. BlueMoon was developed, deployed rapidly, and shared across multiple threat actors within days in a manner that had high detection signals. This may reflect a reduced cost and barrier to entry for this class of capability, as AI agents increasingly enable threat actor exploit development. This is particularly relevant for open source codebases, such as Chromium, where upstream patches are publicly accessible prior to downstream consumers of the codebase applying the patch. This creates a window for threat actors to attempt to rapidly reverse engineer patches and develop exploits ahead of downstream stable releases.

The four groups targeted a wide range of organizations and companies. The groups and targets included:

The first attack came from TA412 and began on August 28. The remainder began earlier this month. Proofpoint said it’s unknown if other groups also gained access to the exploit kit.

Both vulnerabilities targeting Chrome resided in V8, Google’s open source JavaScript engine. Exploiting a V8 type confusion bug and a separate sandbox escape in V8, the attackers were able to execute remote code. They then used a local privilege escalation in older versions of Windows to allow the malicious code to run with system rights. The first V8 vulnerability is tracked as CVE-2026-85046, and the Windows bug is tracked as CVE-2026-85880. Google doesn’t assign CVE designations for V8 sandbox escapes.

“Both V8 vulnerabilities were ‘patch-gap’ zero-days at the time of the observed activity,” Proofpoint said. “In other words, while they were known vulnerabilities already fixed in public upstream Chromium source code, they remained unpatched in the latest stable releases of Chrome and Chromium-based browsers available to the public. It is likely that the exploit kit developer used these publicly available Chromium patches to weaponize the browser exploit chain.”

Although BlueMoon leaves plenty of indications that it’s being used and all three vulnerabilities have been patched, Proofpoint said the kit may nonetheless continue to be used. “Given its ease of adoption, it is likely to proliferate further and be adopted by espionage-motivated and financially motivated threat actors as patched versions are fully rolled out across all Chromium-based browsers,” the researchers said.

items.title: Apple Watch’s new AI features are normalizing the idea that technology is always listening
items.summary: Apple says its new watches won’t save raw audio, but features that can transcribe recent speech and summarize ambient conversations raise new questions about consent, privacy, and how people behave when they know they could always be recorded.
items.content:
Apple is trying to get consumers to accept, and even welcome, a new reality: Your tech is always listening.

At Wednesday’s “Surprise and Shine” iPhone event, where the company introduced its new hardware lineup, the real surprise turned out not to be the foldable iPhone , but how the famously privacy-sensitive tech giant has decided its watches will now be able to process live audio and transcribe what was said.

Does this mean you’re always being recorded if the person you’re interacting with is wearing an Apple Watch? Not exactly — though it may make some people uncomfortable regardless.

It also raises the question of whether consumers actually want this technology, or if Apple forged ahead in this area because it was afraid that another company, such as OpenAI, would soon introduce a competitive AI device of its own.

Today, a number of startups are acting on the belief that AI-powered transcription is a key consumer use case for AI. So far, this more often involves transcribing meeting notes or recording lectures or interviews. Some companies, like the AI pendant Friend and Amazon’s Bee, ventured into other areas, too, with always-available AI companions that can help you remember your day by passively taking notes.

Apple decided to go a slightly different route. With its new watches’ “audio intelligence,” “Live Rewind,” and “Siri Recap” features, the company is straddling the line between accessibility and utility on one side, and what starts to feel like invasive technology on the other.

On its own, Audio Intelligence seems to be a useful feature for the deaf or hard of hearing, as it can alert Apple Watch owners to sounds like sirens, alarms, doorbells, babies crying, and more, using on-device AI. This can work even when the wearer’s iPhone is not with them and, in some cases, could provide life-saving assistance, such as when a fire alarm or carbon monoxide detector goes off. It’s doubtful anyone would take issue with this type of audio AI.

However, Live Rewind and Siri Recap move out of the assistive tech space and into a murkier area.

While Apple’s data protections may make these features more palatable to some, there’s still the possibility that normalizing listening technology may not be the best move for a privacy-conscious company. This is especially true given the broader consumer backlash against surveillance technology like Flock cameras , AI data centers, and AI apps in general .

For starters, the Live Rewind AI feature lets you go back in time 15 seconds and transcribe what was just said by double-pressing the watch’s digital crown. This transcription can then be saved to Apple’s new standalone Siri app so you can revisit the information later.

Apple suggests that this could be used to remember things like a “book recommendation, a colleague’s brilliant idea, or something you didn’t hear the first time,” but it also means that you can essentially catch anyone saying something they didn’t necessarily mean to have recorded and make a note of it.

This has implications around consent, not only from an ethical standpoint but from a legal one as well. AI device-maker Plaud , for instance, advises customers to obtain legally required consent before recording. Amazon’s Bee ‘s terms of service remind users that they’re solely responsible for complying with the law around minors’ data privacy, not Amazon.

Since Apple isn’t saving audio, it’s unclear how the court system might handle these new, text-only transcripts. It’s possible the notes could be introduced as evidence in court, but their lack of audio could make them harder to authenticate or verify. Plus, the evidentiary rules around their use will also likely vary by state.

Beyond the legal issues, the idea that someone can always record from their watch has cultural implications.

Already, recording devices have impacted the way people behave in real life, studies have shown , as has social media and data surveillance culture . Knowing you could be recorded at any time has a dampening effect on how you interact with others and engage in self-expression.

However, recording a photo or video still requires a fairly obvious move on the recorder’s part: you have to hold up your phone and face it toward the action. Snapping up a bit of audio to turn into a transcript just by pressing the watch’s digital crown is arguably a much subtler gesture, even though it comes with an audible chime and full-screen animation of a microphone, as Apple says .

Another new Apple Watch feature, “Siri Recap,” uses ambient listening to “take high-level notes” of your conversations, which can be reviewed in the Siri iOS app. These notes will automatically generate a title, summary, and key points based on what was recorded and summarized by AI. They will not be exact transcripts.

Apple suggests this could make sense for recording meeting takeaways or key info from a parent-teacher conference, for instance.

The company also tried to assure users that it has approached these listening features with respect for user privacy.

Apple notes that Siri Recap doesn’t default to always being on like some other AI wearables are. Instead, you can choose when it’s enabled, like only at work or only during the day. Plus, you can turn the feature off and on at any time from Control Center.

Notably, Apple points out that it does not create or store audio recordings, and that the raw audio isn’t accessible, even to Apple. It also doesn’t identify or attribute the speakers, and it protects the generated transcripts and recaps with end-to-end encryption.

Whether that’s enough for consumers not to feel like the feature is creepy is another matter. Either Apple has found the right balance between utility and privacy, or it’s about to see some consumer backlash.

items.title: Six Chinese AI firms accused of aggressively copying US frontier models
items.summary: US urges AI firms to ID, then secretly switch, Chinese users to less-capable models.
items.content:
The United States has now named six Chinese AI firms accused of waging industrial-scale attacks distilling US frontier AI model capabilities and perhaps sparing billions in Chinese development costs.

In a joint release Tuesday, the National Security Agency (NSA), Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA), and Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) alleged that DeepSeek, Moonshot AI, Alibaba, MiniMax, StepFun, and Z.AI have been attacking US models since at least late 2024. The firms “likely” acted with “Chinese government awareness” when extracting capabilities from US models, including variants of Claude, GPT, Gemini, and Grok, agencies said.

“China-based AI companies that conduct industrial-scale distillation against US AI models see significantly shorter AI development timelines and reduced financial expenditures in training a frontier model,” agencies said.

All American AI firms must work with the government and US allies to end the alleged theft threatening the US lead in the AI race, the agencies said. That will require coordinated action across the AI ecosystem to combat the “aggressive, malicious, and targeted distillation activities at an industrial scale that extract restricted proprietary functionalities and capabilities of US frontier AI models.”

Attack methods include “exploiting AI model inference APIs” by bulk-buying fake accounts, agencies said. Not registered to legitimate users, these swarms of fraudulent accounts execute “highly coordinated queries featuring identical or similar prompt texts,” which range “from thousands to millions on similar topics.”

Another common method is using prompt injection techniques to jailbreak models, including crafting “prompts forcing models to reveal their hidden [chain-of-thought] reasoning,” agencies said. For example, “DeepSeek employed prompts instructing models to imagine and articulate the internal reasoning behind completed responses and write it out step by step.”

To encourage firms to work together, agencies recommended mitigations that would supposedly make it harder for Chinese firms to steal from US models.

First, AI firms must improve detection of sophisticated campaigns that allegedly use tens of thousands of accounts relying on “a gray market of proxies” to evade geographical restrictions and “route distillation requests through multiple pathways to gain unauthorized access.”

Flagging this activity should be somewhat easy, agencies suggested, since “campaigns span days to months with query volumes in the thousands to millions per domain, far exceeding legitimate research or development use cases.”

Generally, they’ve recommended stepping up monitoring for “anomalous and malicious prompts, accounts, networks, and behaviors.” Because Chinese firms rely on “bulk procurement of the US AI companies’ premium subscriptions shared across teams of developers,” that effort should also include flagging accounts with suspicious subscription-to-usage ratios, as well as any new accounts immediately hitting maximum usage, agencies said. Both indicate “bulk deployment with pre-engineered templates,” agencies said. US firms should also be strengthening “identity verification” of users and more closely tracking individuals using enterprise subscriptions (both of which potentially raise privacy red flags for legitimate users).

Next, agencies asked firms to start dumbing down model responses when suspected distillation attacks are flagged. By “subtly” altering responses—such as by “presenting correct information with different reasoning,” adding stylistic inconsistencies, or reducing reasoning depth—firms can decrease the payoff for Chinese firms. US firms could also secretly switch malicious accounts to an inferior model, and they should do so without providing any notice, agencies suggested.

That particular mitigation step will likely be technically challenging.

The agencies acknowledged, for example, that Chinese firms “employ aggressive, adaptive discovery to systematically identify valuable extractable data,” which they then collect to generate synthetic training datasets. Some firms can automatically detect when a smarter model is available and switch within 24 hours. They also have automated quality assurance systems that detect when outputs are degraded and can otherwise differentiate ordinary “service issues from defensive data degradation,” the agencies said.

Also problematic: if US firms aren’t careful with targeting, any legitimate users perhaps caught up in the policing frenzy might be switched to a dumber model without receiving any alert. Or they could suddenly receive shorter responses or experience withheld capabilities, agencies acknowledged. Additionally, firms may add “noise” to the output that restricts further queries. Users will likely notice if outputs degrade, just like Chinese systems attacking models would. Last year, OpenAI quickly made changes to its automatic routing system after facing swift backlash when that system “consistently defaulted to less capable variants unless users explicitly added phrases like ‘think harder’ to their prompt,” Ars reported .

Still, agencies think it’s best practice to “avoid informing China-based AI company users suspected of distillation campaigns of a switch to a downgraded model.”

Acknowledging that such steps could frustrate users, agencies said that firms should try to “balance security with user experience” while accepting that some trade-offs, like “lower prediction precision and business usefulness,” may be inevitable to keep China from copying US capabilities. However, US firms should strive to ensure that “AI safety researchers and third-party evaluators” are “informed of model changes,” agencies suggested.

items.title: Apple's long-rumored foldable becomes reality with the $2,000 iPhone Duo
items.summary: Apple's first foldable can be yours next month.
items.content:
Apple ended today’s hardware event with one of its classic “One more thing” reveals. Some smartphone makers have been offering foldable phones for the better part of a decade, but Apple has now joined the fray with the iPhone Duo after years of speculation .

This device is undeniably the most capable iPhone ever, as well as the most expensive. It’s not as spendy as many expected, though, starting at $1,999. That’s in the same range as foldables from Google and Samsung.

The iPhone Duo would have looked like a totally fresh take on the foldable design a few months ago, but Samsung has made waves with the Galaxy Z Fold 8 . Like that phone, the iPhone Duo has a wider, shorter chassis. Apple prefaced its reveal with a denunciation of foldables that open into a square aspect ratio. While that shape can accommodate two portrait apps side by side pretty well, it’s bad at almost everything else, stretching single apps awkwardly and leaving videos with gargantuan black bars.

So the iPhone Duo adopts a passport-like shape when closed. Apple says the device has a 1:1.4 aspect ratio when open and closed. The 5.4-inch outer screen has a quirky asymmetric design, with pointy corners on the hinge side and rounded ones on the other. Apple suggests this “invites you to open” the phone.

Inside, you get the 7.6-inch Super Retina XDR foldable panel, which is slightly wider than a classic 4:3 monitor. Apple also had a thing or two to say about the structural issues with past foldables. The Duo’s screen contains multiple layers of flexible glass and a titanium base, similar to Samsung’s latest foldable screen tech. The top layer is a custom polymer that is stiffer than other materials, featuring a nano-texture finish for added readability.

The result, allegedly, is a foldable screen that looks better in bright light and has no (or very little) visible crease down the middle. Samsung and other OEMs have only recently gotten to the point where display creases are less noticeable, but they’re still there. Apple also claims the multi-layer lamination process used in its display ensures the display won’t develop a crease over time.

Apple promises the phone, which has the same A20 Pro chip as the new flat phones, will still offer solid battery life. The inner display can play video for 31 hours, and the outer screen can do it for 44 hours. With mixed use of both screens, you can expect the iPhone Duo to last about 24 hours on a charge.

The device has a titanium frame, something Apple briefly experimented with for its flat flagship phones, but this time it has added internal ceramic fibers for even more resilience. The added strength helps with the durability of a device you’re going to be opening and closing all day, but it will also probably make the device pretty heavy. Apple also notes that it has reinforced the antenna lines in the frame to reduce the possibility of failure.

The titanium hinge contains more than 100 components to provide what Apple assures us is a smooth and reliable opening experience with “custom variable torque.” There are also magnets in the frame so the two halves snap together in a satisfying fashion when closed. The device is also IP68 rated for water and dust-resistance.

Interestingly, the iPhone Duo will have a few features that Samsung supported and then abandoned in its foldables. There’s a selfie camera under the foldable screen, which is only visible when in use. Apple also says that the inner and outer screen will support the Apple Pencil later this year. Samsung dropped both those features starting in its 2025 foldable lineup.

The version of iOS on the Duo has also gotten a few enhancements with the foldable form factor in mind. Apple has made it easier to split-screen apps and manage them as a single multitasking unit. The UI and features can also adapt to the hinge position, for example, activating a split keyboard layout when you bend the phone slightly.

Apple has also smartly repositioned some important system elements to take advantage of the wider screens. The home screen app dock and the status bar have moved to the right edge of the screen. Likewise, apps can reposition buttons and controls to the right when you open the phone. This makes these elements easier to reach while preserving the phone’s limited vertical space for content.

Apple crows that the Duo is the thinnest iPhone ever when open, but that’s only true if you ignore the sizable camera plateau on the back. You won’t get the same camera experience as cheaper iPhones, though. In standard foldable fashion, Apple had to downgrade the cameras a bit. There are only two rear-facing sensors, a 48MP primary that lacks the adjustable aperture of the new iPhone 18 Pro, as well as a 12MP with 2x telephoto zoom. There’s a 12MP selfie camera in the outer display in addition to the under-display camera inside.

A $2,000 phone is objectively very expensive, but Apple doesn’t just do expensive—it does lavishly, obscenely expensive. Remember the $3,500 Vision Pro , which cost several times more than competing VR headsets? Yet the iPhone Duo is smack in the middle of high-end foldable pricing.

At $1,999 for the 256GB model, that’s $100 more than the Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8 or Google Pixel 11 Pro Fold and $100 less than Samsung’s square-shaped Z Fold 8 Ultra . Of course, the Duo’s price skyrockets as you start looking at more storage. The 512 model jumps to $2,199, and the 2TB tops out at $3,199.

Apple’s probably not going to get a lot of people to upgrade from their base iPhone 17 to a $2,000 foldable, but matching the price of other tablet-style foldables could put the Duo in a strong position to steal away foldable fans. It’s all rather un-Apple-like.

The iPhone Duo will be available for preorder on October 16 and will ship on October 23.

items.title: Apple debuts $129 AirPods 5 with better noise cancellation and transparency mode
items.summary: AirPods 5 with noise cancellation is cheaper than its predecessor.
items.content:
Apple has debuted the new AirPods 5 with improved active noise cancellation and sound quality—aiming to provide improved listening and user features at a lower launch price than the predecessor AirPods 4.

The newest AirPods will go on sale for $129 in stores starting on September 18, according to an Apple press release accompanying the company’s “Surprise and Shine” event. Customers can also purchase AirPods 5 with a wireless charging case that provides longer battery life and on-stem volume control for $149. Preorders are already open.

This is looking like a solid deal compared to the predecessor AirPods 4. The older AirPods debuted in 2024 with a starting price of $129, but users had to pay $179 for the version with active noise cancellation.

The new AirPods 5 come with active noise cancellation that supposedly removes up to 50 percent more noise in comparison with the AirPods 4—an improvement that Apple credits to a new multiport acoustic architecture and better computational audio algorithms.

Improved transparency mode for the AirPods 5 also allows users to more naturally hear nearby sounds in their immediate vicinity, like people’s voices.

The device’s adaptive audio automatically shifts between active noise cancellation and transparency mode depending on the background noise, said Dave Pakula, VP of hardware engineering for Apple, during the Apple presentation.

A conversation awareness feature also automatically lowers media volume playing through the AirPods when the user starts speaking.

Apple also described boosting the sound quality for AirPods 5 to accommodate “an even wider range of ear geometries,” which it claims will make the personalized spatial audio feel more immersive.

Customers who pay for the AirPods 5 with the wireless charging case will get access to a volume swipe feature that allows them to swipe up and down on the AirPods stem to change the sound level.

The baseline battery life for AirPods 5 enables up to five hours of playback with active noise cancellation activated on a single charge, which exceeds the older AirPods model by one hour. The combination of the charging case and AirPods 5 can extend listening time with ANC to up to 22 hours, and the charging case also supports Apple Watch chargers, Qi-compatible chargers, and USB-C.

Last but not least, the AirPods 5 launch benefits from the latest Apple Intelligence features for iPhone users. Pakula highlighted Siri AI features that play well with AirPods, such as live translation and the ability for AirPods users to respond to Siri by either nodding their head for yes or shaking their head for no.

items.title: Apple starts preorders for Watch Series 12, Ultra 4 with new Health Sensing System
items.summary: New Apple Intelligence features, too.
items.content:
Apple announced the Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4 today. Both include a new “Health Sensing System” and S11 chip that give the devices the “most accurate heart rate sensing in a wearable,” Apple claimed during its fall event .

Both watches will use the new S11 chip alongside the new “Health Sensing System,” allowing the watches to deliver higher-frequency heart rate and heart rate variability (HRV) measurements than prior Apple Watches.

The Health Sensing System includes redesigned photodiodes organized in a ring to capture light more efficiently and a larger electrode surface area for better skin contact. Additionally, the green LEDs on each Watch’s optical heart sensor are supposed to be bigger and more power-efficient and measure the user’s heart rate every five seconds. Users will be able to view their heart rate in real time with a new heart rate watch face special feature (also known as a complication ).

The new watches can take HRV measurements up to 24 times more frequently than their predecessors, Apple said. HRV is an indicator of how well the body is able to adapt to changes such as stress and exercise.

“Overnight vitals now includes recovery HRV measurements analyzed against a user’s personal baseline, providing a more complete view of their health status. A new daytime vitals view lets users toggle between overnight and daytime metrics, and can potentially spot shifts in their metrics before they show up overnight,” Apple said in a press release.

Apple claims that the new wearables have the most accurate heart rate sensing in any wearable based on a study “on a diverse population of over 1,000 participants.”

The new Watches will also introduce “readiness” scores, which Apple says “analyze a user’s recent activity, training load, vitals, and sleep score to offer insight into their capacity for the day ahead” on a scale from 0 to 10. This score updates throughout the day based on the user’s activity.

Apple will update the iOS Health app later this year, allowing Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4 users to access a new “Health Age” score.

“The Health app also includes movement evaluations that measure flexibility, strength, balance, and more using vision-based AI models on iPhone and heart rate data from Apple Watch. Users will be able to schedule and purchase new labs that feature over 50 key biomarkers for $119 directly through the Health app at approximately 2,000 Quest Diagnostics locations in the US,” Apple said.

Apple is also incorporating more Apple Intelligence-based features into the new watches. These features include the ability to use the Shazam song detection feature, Live Rewind, which Apple said “shows the previous 15 seconds of a conversation as a text snippet” when users double-press the Digital Crown, and Siri Recap, which, per Apple, “can create high-level summaries of conversations that users can review later to jog their memory.”

Both watches are available for preorder today and will ship on September 18. The Watch Series 12 starts at $399, and the Ultra 4 starts at $799.

items.summary: Article URL: https://www.apple.com/newsroom/2026/09/apple-introduces-airpods-5-with-best-in-class-open-ear-active-noise-cancellation/ Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49630253 Points: 480 # Comments: 408
